items.text: Somebody filmed on camera two elderly Polish men going up an escalator at a shopping centre the wrong way. They decided to go for a hit after an announcement of free burgers. A large group of people watched as both of them stumbled and fell on the escalator. They eventually made it to the top and received cheers from the crowd. Let’s just hope that the painful climb was worth it. Difficult words: announcement (saying something officially to people), stumble (trip or lose balance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Two elderly men were walking down an escalator when somebody shouted, “Free burgers!” The men, as well as others, wanted the burgers, and the men started to run up the escalator the wrong way. It was not easy for them to get to the top. They tripped and fell several times. The people at the Polish shopping centre filmed and watched the two men. After they finally reached the top, they received cheers from the crowd. Difficult words: elderly (old), trip (to hit something with your foot by accident so that you lose balance), several (a few), cheer (a shout of happiness). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This happens at a shopping centre. The shopping centre is in Poland. Two men are on an escalator . They are going down. Suddenly , somebody shouts, “Free burgers!” The men want the burgers. They must turn around. They must run up the escalator. They are going the wrong way. This is not easy for the men. They fall a few times. People watch them. They film them, too. In the end, the men get to the top. People start to cheer . Difficult words: escalator (moving stairs), suddenly (quickly and without warning), a few (some), cheer (to show that you are happy by saying something loudly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the US, a large dog rescue mission saved around 4,000 from drug tests and experiments. In May, people sued a Virginia facility called Envigo RMS for multiple acts of animal cruelty. Inspectors found the dogs had food with maggots and feces , nursing mother beagles had no food, some of the animals died from easily treated conditions, and 25 puppies died from cold exposure. Now, the effort is to find the dogs good homes. Many of the animals show signs of trauma , they had never felt grass before, and some of the puppies didn’t know how to be held or play. However, according to the US Humane Society, people are overwhelming the shelters because they want to adopt the dogs. Difficult words: maggot (a very small insect that usually feeds on decaying meat and plants), feces (the solid waste of the body), trauma (emotional or physical harm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, a large dog rescue missions happened in Virginia, US, when animal rescue teams saved around 4,000 beagles. The dogs were in a lab to test drugs and do other experiments. Government inspectors closed the lab because the workers treated the animals very badly. The dogs didn’t get enough food and they ate maggots and feces , 25 puppies died because of cold, workers didn’t give medicine to sick animals, and killed some of them. Now, it’s necessary to find a new home for the dogs, but there are many people, who want to adopt them. Some animals never felt grass before, and puppies don’t know how to play. Difficult words: inspector (a person who checks that people follow official rules and laws), maggot (a small insect that eats old meat or plants), feces (the stuff that leaves the body after you eat). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Some people use animals for experiments. People test drugs or makeup on animals. A lab in Virginia, US, treats their animals very badly. Workers at the lab kill sick animals. They don’t give them medicine. Some animals don’t get enough food. They eat maggots. A maggot is a small insect. It eats old meat or plants. 25 dogs die from cold. Inspectors close the lab. Animal rescue groups save 4,000 dogs. Some dogs don’t know how to play. They never see grass before. They will get a new home soon. Many people want to care for the dogs. Difficult words: lab (a place where people do experiments), inspector (a person who checks that people follow rules), animal rescue (an organization which saves animals to find new homes for them). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Mountain bike trials is a discipline of mountain biking in which the rider attempts to pass through an obstacle course without setting foot to ground. Belgian mountain bike trials cyclist and world champion Kenny Belaey managed to bike across a slackline 120-metres above the ground while suspended between two mountains in the French Alps. His first attempt at crossing the stomach-churning course was not successful, but he had another try with his safety harness . Difficult words: obstacle (something in your way), course (a route, way), slackline (a rope used for slacklining – balancing on a not tight rope). stomach – churning (extremely unpleasant and making you feel sick), safety harness (a rope which catches you if you fall). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A man performed a stunt in the French Alps at an altitude of 2,700 metres. People hung a slackline between two mountains 112 metres high in the air. The man tried to ride on a bike from one side to the other. He fell during his first try, but he wore a harness , so he got back up and tried again. This time, he was successful. Difficult words: stunt (a dangerous action), slackline (a rope which is not tight), harness (security rope). You can read the original story and watch the video in the Level 3 section.

This happens in the French Alps. A rope is between two mountains. It is 112 metres in the air. A man is on one of the mountains. He has a bike. He wants to bike to the other mountain. He rides slowly on the rope, but he falls. He is OK. He wears a harness . He gets back up, and he tries again. This time, he is successful . Difficult words: rope (a long piece of textile; line), harness (a security rope), successful (if you are successful, you do something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Northwest of Paris, France, rescuers sadly euthanized a beluga whale that had spent a week in the Seine River. During an unprecedented rescue mission to save the mammal , the 80-person rescue team sent a crane to lift the four-meter and 800-kilogram animal out of the water. The distressed animal swum 100 kilometers inland, it refused to eat, and it became dangerously thin. During a transfer to the Normandy Coast, it had breathing problems, and its health worsened. The animal was obviously in pain; therefore, veterinarians decided to euthanize it. The beluga whale is an extremely sociable animal which lives in groups of up to hundreds of whales. It’s a protected species, and it usually lives in much colder Arctic waters. Difficult words: euthanize (to put an animal to death because it’s sick), unprecedented (never done before), mammal (an animal that nourishes its young with milk). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Northwest of Paris, France, A beluga whale managed to swim 100 kilometers inland and then became trapped in the Seine River. The animal spent a week in the river, and it didn’t eat, so it became very thin and weak. A team of 8 rescuers lifted the animal out of the river with a crane . The animal was four meters long, and it weighed 800 kilograms. Rescuers never did this rescue before. They put the beluga on a truck to transport it to the Normandy Coast. On the way, the animal sadly had more health problems, and it was in pain. Veterinarians decided to end its life because the animal was too sick to return to the sea. Belugas are very social, and they live in groups of hundreds of whales. They prefer cold Arctic waters, and they rarely swim in other places. Difficult words: become trapped (to be unable to leave), crane (a tall machine which lifts and moves heavy things), veterinarian (an animal doctor). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A beluga is a whale. It is small and white. It lives in cold Arctic waters. Hundreds of belugas usually live together. The animal is very sociable . A beluga gets to the French river of Seine. The animal stays a week there. It swims one hundred kilometers. The whale doesn’t eat. It is scared. It is very weak. Rescuers want to help the animal. They want to help it get to the sea. A team of 80 people work together. They use a crane . They lift the animal and put it on a truck . They take it to the Normandy Coast. This work never happens before. The animal becomes very sick during the drive. Veterinarians decide to end its life. It is too sick to go to the sea. Difficult words: sociable (a person or animal who likes to be with others), crane (a tall machine which lifts and moves things), truck (a big car that moves big and heavy things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the context of the whole universe, our solar system is absolutely tiny . Furthermore, it is never illustrated or modelled to scale because if you were to illustrate the system on paper, the planets would actually be microscopic, and therefore invisible. Filmmaker friends Wylie Overstreet and Alex Gorosh made an amazing video of our solar system by creating a 7-mile model in the Nevada, USA, desert. The planets for the ‘true illustration of our place in the universe’ were represented by marbles and spheres lit by LED lights. The representative orbits of the planets were mapped out using GPS calculations, and the planets were driven around these paths in the desert at night. A time-lapse video filmed from a nearby mountain shows every sphere’s orbit. Difficult words: tiny (very small), to scale (at a comparable size), marble (a small ball of coloured glass), sphere (ball). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There is a lot which we don’t know about the universe. What we know is that it’s really, really big. The solar system, for example, is extremely small compared to the whole universe. Two filmmaker friends said that every picture of the Solar System is wrong – the pictures are not to scale . The friends decided to make a model which is to scale. They created the model in the Nevada desert. A marble represented each planet, and each marble was lit by a LED light. The planets moved around in the desert at night. The filmmakers turned this into a film. Go check it out! Difficult words: to scale (if things on a map are to scale, they are as small or as big as they should be compared to other things on the map), marble (a small ball of coloured glass), verb: light – lit – lit . You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The universe is really big. The solar system is big, too. However, it is very small compared to the universe. Two friends make a model. It is a model of the solar system. This model is very big. The men make it in the Nevada desert. They make this model because it is accurate . It shows the real size of the planets. This is what makes the model special. It is the only model which is this accurate. The friends film the model. You can see the planets move. Go check it out! Difficult words: universe (everything which exists in space; the cosmos), solar system (the sun and planets like Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars), compared to (if you compare to things, you put them close together and see how big or small they are), accurate (an accurate model shows you things correctly). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After a record rainfall, flash floods stranded about 1,000 people in California’s Death Valley National Park, one of the world’s hottest and driest spots. A torrential shower unleashed the floods and at least 4.3 centimeters of rain fell at Furnace Creek. By comparison, the park’s average annual rainfall is 4.8 centimeters, which makes it the driest place in North America. Furnace Creek has the record for the highest temperature ever recorded on Earth at 56.7 degrees Celsius. Flash floods from summer rains are a natural part of Death Valley’s ecology , and they shape its dramatic canyon landscape. However, floods of such scale last happened in August 2004, and they killed two people and forced a 10-day closure of all the roads. Difficult words: torrential shower (rain that falls rapidly and with force), unleash (to cause something strong or violent to happen), ecology (plants, animals, water, and geology). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Flash floods hit Death Valley in California, US, and trapped about 1,000 people. Death Valley is one of the hottest and driest places in the world. Experts recorded the highest temperature ever there, which was 56.7 degrees Celsius. Around only 4.8 centimeters of rain falls a year. Last week, 4.3 centimeters of rain fell. Local authorities closed all the roads into the park for several hours. Floods are usual in Death Valley, but they happen at different places. They are the reason for the canyon in the valley. The last strong flood happened in 2004. It killed two people and closed the roads for ten days. Difficult words: flash flood (a sudden flood, which usually happens because of heavy rain), valley (a low area between two hills or mountains), canyon (a very deep and narrow space between two mountains, usually with a stream flowing through). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Death Valley is a place in California, US. It is one of the driest and hottest places on earth. People measure the highest temperature ever here. It is 56.7 degrees Celsius. The valley is dry. Around 4.8 centimeters of rain fall here every year. Last week, flash floods happen. 4.3 centimeters of rain fall in a very short time. 1,000 people are in the valley. They can’t leave. Authorities close all roads. Floods happen every year in Death Valley. They happen in different places. They shape the valley. In 2004, a flood kills two people. Difficult words: measure (to find out the size, amount, distance, and so on), flash flood (a very strong amount of water after a heavy rain), shape (to make something look in a certain way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Whole Body Cryotherapy is New York’s latest health and fitness trend, which is meant to boost metabolism and help the body heal itself. The treatment, which people developed in Japan and people have used in parts of Europe for about twenty years, means that you have to submerse yourself in extremely low temperatures of -130 degrees Celsius. Cryotherapy works by making the brain believe that the body is freezing, which then goes into survival mode and begins to send blood, enriched with oxygen, enzymes and nutrients, to the body’s core. In one of New York’s spa, customers pay about 90 US dollars for a three-minute treatment. They wear a bathing suit, socks and gloves to protect themselves from acute frostbite while liquid nitrogen is used to cool the air in the chamber. Difficult words: metabolism (how fast the body uses food), submerse (cover completely). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This news is about whole body cryotherapy . It is a form of therapy which helps your body to heal . The only problem is that you must spend three minutes in a super cold chamber . The temperature in the chamber is -130 degrees Celsius. Cryotherapy works by making the brain believe that the body is freezing. The body then sends oxygen-rich blood to the centre of the body. This makes you feel great. You feel relaxed and full of energy. Cryotherapy is a big hit in New York. Customers pay about 90 dollars for three minutes. Difficult words: cryo- (involving extreme cold), heal (to become healthy again), chamber (a small room). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is about cryotherapy . This therapy helps your body. It gives you energy. It makes you feel relaxed. First, you must enter a small room. It is extremely cold in the room. It is -130 degrees Celsius in the room. You stay three minutes in this room. Your brain thinks that you are going to freeze . This is good for your body. Cryotherapy is a big hit in New York. Three minutes cost 90 dollars. Difficult words: cryo- (extremely cold), therapy (something which helps you), freeze (died because of a very low temperature). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In April, twelve-year-old Archie Battersbie suffered traumatic brain injuries after an incident at home. Doctors and his family battled in court over whether to continue life-support treatment; however, he died on August 6, 2022. In April, Archie’s mother found him unconscious with a ligature over his head at their home in Essex, UK. She believed that he had taken part in a dangerous TikTok challenge known as the “blackout challenge”. In this challenge, young people hold their breath, or they choke until they become unconscious due to lack of oxygen. Since that time, the boy was in a coma , and doctors kept him alive with life support treatments. Doctors declared him to be brain dead, which began a lengthy legal battle with the boy’s family who wanted treatment for his recovery. A court decided the boy’s best interest was to end the support, which the doctors did last Sunday. Difficult words: ligature (a tightly tied or bound thing), coma (deep unconsciousness when a person responds to nothing, usually because of an injury or illness), best interest (a decision how to take care of someone who cannot choose). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Archie Battersbie was a twelve-year-old boy from Essex, UK. In April this year, his mother found him at their home with a belt around his neck. Archie was unconscious . His mother said that had participated in a dangerous challenge on TikTok. Archie spent four months in a hospital, but he never woke. Doctors said that the boy’s brain was dead, and only the machines kept him alive. They said that Archie would never recover , and they suggested to switch off the machines. Archie’s family didn’t agree, and in the end, a court decided the situation to let him die. Archie’s family fought hard, but doctors switched off the machines last week on Sunday, and then the boy died. The “blackout challenge” on TikTok is popular with young children. They hold their breath or choke , and sometimes they become unconscious. Difficult words: unconscious (not awake and no reaction to anything), recover (to get healthy again), choke (to stop breathing because of something in the throat or no oxygen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Archie Battersbie is twelve years old. He lives with his family in Essex, UK. He is in a TikTok challenge called the “blackout challenge”. Young children like to do the challenge. It is very dangerous. At home, Archie puts a belt around his neck. The belt makes him not breathe. He falls unconscious . His mother finds Archie. He spends four months in hospital. Doctors say that his brain is dead. They say that he will never be healthy again. The boy has no oxygen for too long. Machines keep his body alive. Doctors want to switch off the machines. Archie’s family is against the change. A court must decide. Last Sunday, doctors switch off the machines. The boy dies. Difficult words: challenge (a difficult activity), unconscious (not able to wake), oxygen (a gas in air that people need to live). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chris, an extremely overgrown Australian sheep, set an unofficial world record after living in the wild for several years. Welfare crews warned that he was at risk of dying because he was so woolly. National shearing champion Ian Elkins, who in 35 years of work had never seen anything like this, was urgently called by people to save the sheep. At four to five times the normal size of a regular sheep, Ian and four others sheared off more than 40 kilograms of wool. This was the heaviest wool haul from one shearing. Chris had to be sedated for his big transformation. Difficult words: welfare (the health and happiness of somebody), crews (a group of people working together), haul (something which is collected), sedate (give medicine to keep someone calm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An Australian sheep named Chris was living in the wild for several years. His wool grew so much that it put him at risk of dying. He was four to five times his normal size. People called the national shearing champion for help. Five other shearers and he sedated Chris and gave him a haircut. They removed forty kilograms of wool. Without knowing it, Chris broke a world record. Difficult words: several (a few), shear (to cut wool), sedate (to calm somebody down or make him or her sleep by giving him or her a drug). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Australia. It is about a sheep. His name is Chris. Chris lives in the wild . People do not shear him. His wool just grows and grows. Chris gets really big. He has 40 kilograms of wool on him. Normally, he has 4 to 5 times less wool. Chris is in danger. People must shear him. Five men make him sleep and they shear him. Difficult words: in the wild (in nature not changed by people), shear (to cut wool). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Geologists at the Iowa Geological Survey discovered 150 pieces of fossils of a giant underwater scorpion about 18 metres under the upper Iowa River. The giant underwater creature reigned the ocean almost half a billion years ago, predating even the dinosaurs. It grew up to 170 centimetres in length, had 12 claw arms sprouting from their heads and had a spiked tail. The animal is called Pentecopterus and is part of the Eurypterid family of sea scorpions. Unlike modern land scorpions, its tail did not sting and was used more for balance. There are more than 250 individual species of Eurypterid, but the majority of the discovered specimens are of the Eurypterus species. Difficult words: reign (be dominant), predate (live before), sprout (grow), spiked (with spikes – sharp parts), species (a type of animal), specimen (an individual used as an example of its species). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

American geologists found 150 pieces of fossils about 18 metres under the Upper Iowa River. The fossils belong to a predator which lived 0.5 billion years ago. It was a giant underwater scorpion. It grew up to 170 centimetres in length. However, half of this animal’s length was its tail. It used it for balance. The tail was spiked , but it did not sting like the tail of a modern scorpion. The animal, which is called Pentecopterus, also had 12 arms at the front. Difficult words: fossil (when an animal dies a long time ago and turns into a rock), spiked (with spikes – sharp parts), sting (to attack and make a small hole in your skin). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People find one hundred and fifty pieces of fossils . They find them under a river. The river is in Iowa, USA. The fossils belong to an animal. This animal lived 0.5 billion years ago. It was a predator – an underwater scorpion. It was 170 centimetres long. However, 50% of its body was the tail. The animal had 12 arms at the front. Difficult words: fossil (when an animal dies a long time ago and turns into a rock), was (past of “is”), predator (an animal which catches and eats other animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Before climate change’s impact, the inhabitants of Fiji’s Serua Island thought they would spend all their lives in one place. However, the community is struggling to adapt to the Pacific Ocean’s rise. At high tide, the ocean breaches the sea wall, and it floods the village and people’s gardens. Villagers are facing floods, erosion, and extreme weather; they must decide whether to stay or relocate to Fiji’s main island to secure a future for the next generation. In 2014, a similar community successfully relocated from their old village, which made Fiji the first Pacific Island nation to relocate a community because of sea level rise. Many Fijians believe that developed nations contribute the most to global warming; they want them to curb their emissions and pay for the work that islanders have to do. Difficult words: breach (to break a hole), relocate (to move to a new place to live or start business there), curb (to control the growth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in Fiji are dealing with the rise of ocean levels because of climate change . Many of them must decide if they want to stay in their homeland or to move away. When high tide happens, salt water comes into people’s homes and gardens. The water destroys homes and crops. Many old people still don’t want to leave. Many people in Fiji think that other large countries are responsible for climate change, and they should pay for their new homes. In 2014, one village moved to a new place, but people still return to their old village almost every day. Fiji is the first country which moved a community because of sea level rise. Difficult words: climate change (the changes in weather because of nature and people’s activity), high tide (the time when the sea is at its highest level), community (people who live in the same small place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Fiji have a big problem. Climate change makes sea water go up. The water gets into people’s homes and gardens during high tide . People can’t grow anything. Their homes are destroyed. People must decide what to do. Some people want to move away. Older people want to stay. They live in the village all their lives. In 2014, one community moves away. Their move is the first time that people leave because sea water goes up. People still come back to their old village almost every day. People in Fiji say that they don’t cause the climate change. They want money for new homes from bigger countries. They say that the countries add to climate change. Difficult words: climate change (the changes in weather which come from nature and people), high tide (the time when the sea goes up), community (people who live in one small place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A video went viral that showed 24-year-old Zak Maytum skating down a road in Colorado, USA, at 112 kilometres per hour. The video gained more than a million views in just three days after being uploaded. An organiser of the stunt said that Zak wore padding underneath his clothing so that the viewer could not see it on the video. The stuntman also had a helmet and wore very specific shoes. He had customised the longboard and specially it tuned for high-speed riding. Zak Maytum is one of the professionals in the sport of downhill skateboarding and has been riding for more than a decade. Difficult words: gain (earn), stunt (a dangerous action), padding (soft but tough material for protection), longboard (a type of skateboard that has a very long board to stand on). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On the Internet, someone uploaded a video which went viral . The video shows a 24-year-old man. He is riding a longboard skateboard down a hill in Colorado, USA. He skates at 112 kilometres per hour! It looks like the man wears no helmet or padding in the video, but he does. It is hidden under his clothing so you cannot see it in the video. The professional’s longboard was specially tuned for high speeds. He also wears a pair of special shoes. Difficult words: viral (to be popular), padding (soft but tough material for protection of the body), tune (to make something better for a specific action). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

On the Internet, there is a video. It gets popular very quickly. It shows a man. He is 24 years old. He is riding a longboard skateboard. He is going down a hill. This hill is in Colorado, USA. He skates at 112 kilometres per hour! The man wears a helmet and padding . However, you cannot see them in the video. Difficult words: skate (to move on a skateboard or a longboard), helmet (protection for the head), padding (protection for the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Doctors in Brazil successfully separated three-year-old twins who were born conjoined at the head, and for the first time, the boys were able to lay face-to-face. In 2018, Arthur and Bernardo Lima were born in a rural part of northern Brazil, and they shared part of the brain and main vein that carries blood to the heart. They were the oldest twins with a fused brain to have separation surgery. Doctors spent months researching and preparing for the surgery, and they practiced on virtual reality projections of the twins. For the first time, surgeons in separate countries wore headsets, and they operated in the same virtual reality room together. The twins had seven surgeries, and the final operation involved more than 27 hours of operating time and almost 100 medical staff. Difficult words: conjoined (joined together), fused (joined into one thing), projection (the display of an image on a screen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2018, twins Arthur and Bernardo Lima were born in a Brazilian village. They were not ordinary twins because their heads were joined together. The twins shared part of the brain and the vein which takes blood to the heart. Doctors spent many months to plan a surgery to separate the boys. Thanks to virtual reality, doctors from different countries met and learn how to perform the real surgery. The surgery happened in Rio de Janeiro, and almost 100 medical staff were part of it. Seven surgeries happened altogether, and the final surgery took more than 27 hours. After the surgery, the boys could finally look at each other. Difficult words: ordinary (usual), vein (a body part that looks like a tube and carries the blood through the body), final (the last). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2018, twins are born in a Brazilian village. They are Arthur and Bernardo Lima. They look different from other twins. Their heads are joined together . The boys share a part of the brain and a body part. This part takes blood to the heart. Doctors think that they can separate the boys. The work is hard. They spend many months to plan a surgery . Virtual reality helps doctors. Doctors from different countries meet in one virtual reality room. The boys have seven surgeries altogether. The last surgery is more than 27 hours long. The surgery is successful. The twins can look at each other for the first time. Difficult words: twin (one of two children, who are born to one woman at the same time), joined together (things which touch each other and share parts), separate (to take apart), surgery (work when a doctor cuts the body open and fixes it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fully automated self-driving cars are no longer the imagination of the distant future. Thanks to companies like Waymo, cars are already driving around in some cities. Since 2016, the American autonomous car producer has been testing its self-driving cars on the streets of Arizona, US. The company’s mission is to make it safe and easy for people to use the cars, and it believes that AV technology can improve road safety. In the US, the fatality rate in car accidents increased over the last few years, and human error is a majority cause. Waymo has autonomously driven over 32 million kilometers on public roads and over 30 billion kilometers in simulation, and according to data, its cars were involved only in minor collisions. The company believes that the data is evidence of the safety benefits of autonomous vehicles, and it’s the first company to provide a commercial ride hailing service. Difficult words: human error (a person’s mistake rather than a machine failure), minor (less serious or important), hail (to signal to stop a car, usually a taxi). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2016, American company Waymo started to test its autonomous or self-driving cars. The company said that these cars made roads safer. Waymo’s cars drove over 32 million kilometers on the streets of Arizona, US, and over 30 billion kilometers in simulation . Autonomous cars were involved only in not very serious car accidents. In the US, the number of car crashes and deaths increased in the past years, and often due to human error . Most deaths happened because the driver was drunk, tired, or drove too fast. A self-driving car does not cause these problems; therefore, Waymo believes that its cars make travel for people safer and easier. Waymo is the first company to give taxi service with its cars. People call the Waymo car, it stops, opens the door, and it drives the person whenever he needs. Difficult words: in simulation (to practice a situation to learn to do something in real life), involve (to have something or be part of something), human error (a person’s mistake). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Waymo is an American company. It makes self-driving cars . These cars don’t have no driver. Since 2016, Waymo’s cars drive on a US city’s streets. They drive as taxis . People call a car. The car comes. It opens its doors. The person gets in. The car takes the person to whenever he needs to go. It is the first taxi service to use self-driving cars. Waymo says that its cars make the roads safer. Many car accidents happen because of the driver’s mistake. Sometimes, the driver is tired or drunk . Sometimes the driver is too fast. Self-driving cars don’t have these problems. Waymo’s cars already drive 32 million kilometers. They don’t cause serious accidents. Difficult words: self-driving car (a car that drives itself with no driver), taxi (a car that takes a person somewhere for money), drunk (after you drink alcohol and you cannot do things or think well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A group of fishermen in Peru working in the northwest of the country discovered a huge manta ray which local media said weighs just over a tonne. People said that the ray swam into the fishermen’s net as they trawled for fish in a homemade wooden boat. The enormous , 8-metre creature was found in the La Crove cave in waters near the border with Ecuador. A fisherman said that it was so big, that it could not be loaded onto their boat and had to be transported by a tow truck . In ancient Peru, the manta ray, which is in the same biological order as smaller stingrays, was often represented in art where they were feared because of their size. People believed that they ate fish and sank boats, and it was not until the late 1970’s that perceptions began to change. This was when people realised that they were actually pretty placid and harmless to humans. Difficult words: trawl (pull a trawl net – a large fishing net), enormous (very big), creature (an animal), tow truck (a truck for moving heavy things), perception (the way people think about something), placid (calm and peaceful). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A group of fishermen in Peru caught a huge fish. The fish weighed over a tonne and was eight metres long. People call this type of fish the manta ray. One fisherman described how they caught the fish. It swam into their nets which were towed by their homemade boat. The fish was, of course, too big for their boat, so a tow truck transported it. Sailors believed that manta rays ate fish and sank boats. They were afraid of them. The perception began to change in the late 1970’s – sailors started to understand that manta rays are calm and not dangerous. Difficult words: huge (very big), tow truck (a truck for moving very heavy things), perception (the way people think about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from Peru. A group of fishermen get lucky. They catch a very big fish. It is one tonne heavy. It is eight metres long. This fish is a “manta ray”. The fishermen have a small boat. It is wooden and homemade . The big fish cannot fit on the boat. A tow truck must move the fish. Manta rays are big, but they are not dangerous. They are calm. Difficult words: tonne (1,000 kilograms), homemade (made at home, not bought from a shop), tow truck (a car for moving very heavy things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After months of a blockade , Ukraine has finally begun to ship grain again out of its Black Sea ports, and people hope that the activity will ease global food shortages. According to Ukrainian and Turkish officials, the first grain cargo vessel sailed from the port of Odessa to Lebanon under a safe passage agreement . Russia has blockaded Ukrainian ports since February; however, the two countries decided to resume shipments. Under the deal, Russia has agreed not to target ports while the shipments are in transit . Russia and Ukraine grow nearly a third of the world’s grain exports, and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine worsened the global food crisis. In past years, Ukraine also produced 16% of the world’s corn and 42% of sunflower oil. The blockade of Ukraine’s grain increased prices of wheat-based products like bread and pasta, cooking oil, and fertilizer. Difficult words: blockade (to halt the movement of people and goods into or out of a county), safe passage agreement (a deal to give official protection to pass through a dangerous area), in transit (to carry people or things from one place to another). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

When Russia attacked Ukraine five months ago, Russia blocked Ukraine’s ports in the Black Sea. The action stopped Ukraine’s exports , which badly impacted the global food market and increased the prices of some products. Russia and Ukraine grow nearly one third of the world’s grain. Since the beginning of the war, the prices of products increased such as bread, pasta, and cooking oil. On Monday, the first ship with grain left the Ukrainian port of Odessa. The event happened under a deal between Ukraine and Russia. Russia promised that it wouldn’t attack Ukraine’s ports with cargo ships . Officials hope that this will help the global food crisis. Difficult words: block (to stop something from moving or flowing), export (the trade of things to another country), cargo ship (a ship that takes things and materials from one port to another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ukraine and Russia grow much of the world’s grain . Russia attacks Ukraine in February. Ukraine can’t sell its grain. Ukraine also grows 16% of the world’s corn and 42% of sunflower oil. Russia blocks Ukrainian ports for five months. The world’s prices of food go up. In some countries, the food crisis gets worse. Foods like bread, pasta, or cooking oil cost more money. On Monday, a ship with grain leaves the Ukrainian port of Odessa. The ship is the first to leave since the war starts. Russia and Ukraine make a deal. Russia won’t attack Ukraine’s ports. It will wait only if ships have food there. Officials hope that it will help the global market. Difficult words: grain (wheat or corn which people grow for food), port (a place for ships to sell and buy things), food crisis (a time when people don’t have enough food or the food is too expensive). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A Swiss agricultural institute made a revelation of why Swiss cheese has holes in it: hay. Traditionally, people gather milk via buckets open to the air, and this means that microscopically small particles of hay can get into the milk, which creates holes as the liquid matures into cheese. Through a series of tests, scientists tried adding different amounts of hay dust to milk in the cheese-making process. They found that they could regulate the number of holes. This research also solves another mystery of why the famous holes in cheeses like Emmentaller are getting smaller or disappearing during the last fifteen years. This is due to milk becoming cleaner through the use of industrial milking systems. Difficult words: agricultural (relating to the study of farming), institute (a place that researches and studies different things), revelation (a surprising and unknown fact), particle (a very small thing), mature (get older and change), regulate (control). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

After old stories about hungry mice, many random guesses , and a hundred years of research , we now know why Swiss cheese has holes in it. And mice are not responsible. There are holes in cheese because of hay . Very small particles of hay get into the milk and create holes when the milk turns into cheese. Over the last 15 years, the holes have been getting smaller, or are gone completely. This is thanks to modern milking systems –milk is much cleaner than before. The amount of hay dust added to the milk can control the number of holes. Difficult words: random guess (when you say that something could be true, but you do not really know why), research (scientific study), hay (dried grass which is fed to animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Do you like Swiss cheese? Do you know why there are holes in it? It is not because of hungry mice. It is because of hay . A little bit of hay gets into milk. When the milk turns into cheese, the hay makes the holes. In the past, the holes in cheese were bigger. More hay got into the milk, then. Today, milk is much cleaner. Difficult words: hole (space), hay (dried grass which is given to animals), were (past of “are”). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Firefighters evacuated dozens of people from towns near the Bohemian Switzerland National Park on the Czech Republic’s border with Germany as a wildfire burned out of control. The blaze started on Sunday, and winds and extremely dry conditions pushed it toward Germany. The smoke reached the capital Prague 100 kilometers to the south; however, it was detected as far as 180 kilometers to the south-east. The fire threatened several villages, and firefighters urged tourists to avoid the area. Fires happen in Bohemian Switzerland every year; however, they do not usually happen on such a scale . According to authorities, a negligent camper probably started the blaze. The national park is a popular tourist attraction with its naturally formed sandstone arch, the largest in Europe. The park has featured in a number of moves, including The Chronicles of Narnia. Difficult words: scale (a size), negligent (careless), sandstone (a soft yellow or red rock). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

On Saturday, a fire started suddenly in the Czech Republic’s Bohemian Switzerland National Park. The weather was hot and very dry this summer, and strong winds made the fire spread quickly. The flames moved close to the border with Germany, and both Czech and German firefighters evacuated several villages. Fires happen every summer in the national park, but this fire was much bigger, and authorities said that a camper started it. People as far as 180 kilometers could smell the smoke. The national park is very popular for its sandstone arch, which is the largest in Europe. Sandstone labyrinths and beautiful valleys are there, and around 400,000 tourists visit the park every year. Difficult words: sandstone (a soft yellow or red rock), labyrinth (many paths in which you can get lost), valley (a low area between two hills or mountains). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Bohemian Switzerland National Park is in the Czech Republic. It is close to Germany. The park is very popular with tourists. 400,000 people visit it every year. Beautiful paths are there. People can see tall sandstone mountains. The largest sandstone arch in Europe is there. Also, every summer there are fires. A big fire starts in the park last week. It is bigger than usual. People can smell the smoke 180 kilometers away. Firefighters evacuate several villages. Strong winds bring the fire closer to Germany. Authorities say that a camper starts the fire. He is not careful in the hot and dry weather. Difficult words: sandstone (a soft yellow or red rock), arch (a rock structure which looks like a bridge), evacuate (to take someone to a safe place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Supposedly, your sense of taste diminishes with altitude , but despite that, one astronaut on the International Space Station got creative with her food. Samantha Cristoforetti of the European Space Agency recorded a cooking show while on the ISS and made a meal that we could say was literally out of this world . She made her meal out of champignon mushrooms , peas, chicken, turmeric and other ingredients, and she showed how to cook the food using the tools available to her in the ISS, such as a food warmer and scissors. She commented that her food tasted good despite being in weightlessness . This recipe is a space experiment that you could try at home! Difficult words: diminish (become less), altitude (height), ISS (the abbreviation of the International Space Station), literally out of this world (this is a joke – something that is amazing and something that is in space), champignon mushroom (a type of mushroom that is rare and supposed to taste very good), turmeric (a type of spice), weightlessness (having no weight due to being in space). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An astronaut onboard the International Space Station made her own cooking show while in space. She recorded herself cooking different dishes with food pouches and the tools available to her in space. In one video, she made chicken with turmeric , mushrooms, brown rice, and peas. While she heated some food pouches in the food warmer, she opened other food pouches. At the end of the video, she tried her dish, which she said was not bad for being made in space. Difficult words: food pouch (a special bag that keeps food together until you open the bag), turmeric (a yellow spice. You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An astronaut is on the International Space Station. She likes to cook. She makes her own cooking show. The show is in space. There is a video of her cooking show. On it, she cooks with a couple of ingredients . She cooks chicken, mushrooms, brown rice, and peas. The food is in food pouches . She heats the food pouches . She says that scissors are very important in the space kitchen. She uses them to open the food pouches. She mixes the food together. She eats it. She says that her food is good. Difficult words: ingredients (the things that go in food), food pouch (a special bag to keep food inside in space). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People have been fermenting alcohol for a long time as they enjoy alcohol’s effects, and as it turns out, some animals enjoy it, too! International researchers conducted a 17-year-long empirical study and found that some chimpanzees drink alcohol from leaf vessels . Video footage showed a chimp using leaves to collect fermented sap from a palm tree. The scientists observed the animals in many states of inebriation , including falling asleep after drinking. Difficult words: ferment (turn into alcohol), conduct (run), empirical (based on scientific testing), vessel (a container for holding liquids), fermented (turned into alcohol), sap (the fluid in a plant), inebriation (being drunk). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Many people like a drink from time to time, but it seems that animals enjoy alcohol, too. Scientists thought this for a while, but now, we have proof. Scientists studied the drinking of animals for 17 years. Chimpanzees, for example, use leaves as a sponge to collect fermented sap from palm trees. Then they put the leaves into their mouths to drink the alcohol. Difficult words: sponge (a soft thing which can hold a liquid), fermented (alcoholic), sap (the fluid in a plant). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People like to drink. However, we are not alone. Scientists study animals for 17 years. They now know that animals drink, too. Plants have sap in them. Sap can become alcohol. Chimpanzees drink the alcohol. Difficult words: sap (sweet “water” inside plant which can become alcohol), chimpanzee (a smart animal that is like a large monkey without a tail). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
